messages:
Kai: Heads-up — Marketing confirmed 'Week of Deals' Nov 15-22. Need a quick capacity read + known risks for serving heavy rerank + embedding workloads. Rough spreadsheet forecast says ~4.8k GPU-hours for the week if we see a 1.8x pulse. Any immediate blockers?

Marta: Noted. Do we have region breakdowns? If most traffic hits us-west-2 we might hit burst limits on our reserved fleet.

Kai: Main traffic is north-america (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 fallback), ~70% / 30% split in the projection. EU is negligible for this campaign.

Liam: 4.8k GPU-hours => ballpark 40 extra A100-equivalent GPUs for the busiest 36h window, assuming 90% utilization. That's if we don't change batching or KV cache config.

Priya: Can we reduce by mixing quantized variants and larger batch sizes? Redwood Optimize suggestions earlier hinted 22% token-cost savings for rerank flows when using int8 + aggressive prefix caching.

Marta: We can try: increase batch_size to 64 for rerank where latency SLO is 150ms p50 and 400ms p99. But p99 may climb. Tradeoff: save GPUs but push tail latency.

Zara: Ops question — do we have spare burst capacity in our Dedicated pools or do we need to pre-provision Dedicated capacity and map traffic via routing policies? 

Liam: Dedicated pool has ~12 GPUs free in us-west-2 today. Marketplace transient burst adds ~8ish but unpredictable. To guarantee capacity we should reserve + schedule prewarmed instances 48h before campaign.

Kai: Cost talk: extra 40 A100s reserved for a week is ~ $X/day (finance will get exact), but we can also use policy: route low-priority traffic to cheaper quantized endpoints and set graceful fallback to hosted variants. Thoughts?

Priya: Proposal: hybrid plan — reserve 16 GPUs (dedicated), spin ephemeral spot-backed fleet up to +24 GPUs for peak, and enable routing policy: prioritize dedicated -> hosted-quantized -> hosted-standard. That minimizes cost while bounding guaranteed throughput.

Marta: Sounds reasonable. Need to add network egress considerations — previous campaigns had a small spike in inter-AZ chatty traffic during large batching. Check that VPC peering and NAT throughput won't bottleneck.

Liam: Will run quick network sanity: check ENI counts, NAT GW bandwidth, and any ASG cooldowns that could delay scale-up. Also will validate instance warming: warm model cache with a short synthetic load 6h before launch.

SRE-Bot: @Kai @Marta @Liam Scheduled prewarm run created: run-id=prewarm-177250, starts 2026-11-14T04:00Z, nodes=20, script=/ops/prewarm.sh. Alerts configured for model-load-failures and server OOM.

Zara: Two operational risks to call out: (1) cross-region fallbacks may hit higher latency for users routed from us-west-2 -> us-east-1; decide SLAs. (2) If quantized endpoints under-provide quality, product may roll back mid-week — need eval run and a canary.

Priya: I'll run a small eval set comparing int8 vs fp16 outputs, sample 500 prompts. If quality drop <1.5% measured regressions we go int8; else stick to fp16 and lean on batch/caching.

Kai: Action items: (1) Liam: network & warm plan + spin tests by EOD today. (2) Priya: quality eval + pass/fail threshold by EOD tomorrow. (3) Marta: reserve 16 GPUs in us-west-2 and coordinate finance for week-reserve approval. (4) Zara: add canary route and rollback playbook to the runbook. I'll update the runbook with pricing knobs.

Liam: Ack. I'll post test logs in this thread when done.

Marta: Ack. I'll open the commit with reserved capacity request and tag @Finance.

Priya: Starting eval now, will share a short report.

Kai: Thanks team. Quick note: flag any capacity surprises ASAP. Use #incidents if you see degradation. :thumbsup:
